pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Changed ClaimInfo and claimInfoCache APIs to avoid updating cached claim infos when the cache is not locked.
This should fix possible data race conditions caused by changing cached claim infos.

Added new unit and e2e_node test cases to test cache integrity.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #123474 #116411

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This is a second attempt to fix #123474. See [previous PR](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124284) and  [this review comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124284#discussion_r1565406305) for more details.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
NONE
```

review_comments: Why not just continue to track claimInfos? That way we can remain symmetrical with `UnprepareResources()`
`UnprepareResources` tracks claim names. Both changes decrease usage of claimInfo objects outside of cache operations. I thought that it's much more clear if claimInfo only used when cache is locked.
Then I'd argue we should drop `get()` altogether and perform all operations through the cache once a claimInfo has been added (including things like `Contains()` and `isPrepared()`.
Can you elaborate? Are you talking about `claimInfoCache.get`? I'd love to drop it, but how is it related to this code? This code was added here to avoid using not cached claim infos.
Because it feels odd to me to call `get()` to pull something called `claimInfo` out of the cache, and then not use that to track the info about the claim across the calls.

It looks like it's a matter of taste. claimInfo object is used to check `prepared` field. This saves one lock of cache comparing to your code and I did it to decrease a number of cache locks. However, now I understand what you mean. Will try to do what you've suggested.
Looks like you found a bug when writing the unit tests?
I'm not sure we need these defensive checks. It's probably better to initialize both fields in the new* functions.
I thought you had added them for a reason when adding the unit test (it's in that commit). :shrug:
You can use `maps.Clone` here and then don't need the loop.

Looking again -- this won't work as is. It is racy with the addPodReference() code above.

Consider the two code blocks (which can run concurrently):
```
if cache.contains(...) {
    cache.addPodReference(...)
}
```
and
```
if cache.contains(...) {
    cache.add(...)
}
```

The following sequence is possible:
```
// pod 0
if cache.contains(claim0) // false
if cache.isPrepared(claim0) // false
if cache.contains(claim0) // false

// pod 1
if cache.contains(claim0) // false
if cache.isPrepared(claim0) // false
if cache.contains(claim0) // false

// pod 0
cache.add(claim0Info) // with reference to pod0

// pod 1
cache.add(claim0Info) // with reference to pod1
```
The entry in the cache now only has a reference to pod1 not pod0

@klueska We mark claiminfo as prepared only if `NodePrepareResources` succeeded for all plugins. I think we incorrectly handle the case of partial preparation - when the `NodePrepareResources` succeeded only for some plugins. If pod is deleted, Kubelet will not call `NodeUnprepareResources` for those plugins as this information is not cached.

The `prepared` field is only used to avoid erroneous calls to `PrepareResources` -- `UnprepareResources` doesn't look at it at all. If we have ever created a claimInfo object and added a pod reference to it, we _will_ get an `UnprepareResources` call for it (either in sync with the deletion or in the reconcile loop).
It makes sense to me now. Thanks for the explanations.
